result.title: Fractional is Better: Learnable Derivative Orders in Neural Operator Learning
result.comment: Accepted at ICML 2026. 37 pages, 11 figures, 13 tables. Code: https://github.com/FaresBMehouachi/delNO
result.summary: Neural operators learn mappings between function spaces, enabling fast surrogate solutions to partial differential equations. Despite remarkable architectural diversity, these methods often share a common input representation: raw coordinate-value pairs $(x, u(x))$. We ask whether inputs aligned with PDE differential structure can improve learning. Through Picard iteration on mild solutions, we show that derivatives of the input appear explicitly in the solution operator, suggesting that providing derivative features should reduce the network's implicit differentiation burden. We prove this intuition: providing derivative features improves approximation bounds from $O(W^{-(s-m)/d})$ to $O(W^{-s/d})$, where $W$ is parameter count, $s$ is input regularity, $m$ is the PDE order, and $d$ is spatial dimension. Our central finding, however, is a surprise: the optimal derivative order $β^*$ is strictly less than the PDE order $m$. This gap arises from a bias-variance tradeoff in spectral space that we characterize in closed form. Learning $β$ from data achieves automatic spectral regularization. We introduce $\partial$-NO (del-NO), for derivative-augmented neural operators, an architecture-agnostic augmentation that provides learnable fractional derivative features to any neural operator backbone. Across benchmark problems and architectures, $\partial$-NO consistently improves prediction accuracy, with learned orders that reflect a representation of known physics modulated by noise and finite-sample constraints.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究神经算子是否应输入与 PDE 微分结构对齐的特征：证明提供导数特征可改进逼近界，并发现最优导数阶 β* 严格小于 PDE 阶 m，源于谱空间的偏差—方差取舍，进而提出可学习分数阶导数特征的架构无关增强 ∂-NO。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「可学习连续阶数 + 闭式谱空间偏差—方差分析」可能为 LVR 中「显式特征该注入多少、latent 状态如何被自动正则化」提供类比视角，可供核查；但研究对象为 PDE 算子代理，与视觉多模态推理链路较远。
